# Implementation Plan: Scanned Form to Completed PDF Workflow

**Branch**: `001-scanned-form-workflow` (no git branch, commit, or publication is created by this plan) | **Date**: 2026-11-12 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-scanned-form-workflow/spec.md`; ratified constitution from `.specify/memory/constitution.md` (v1.0.0, no amendment requested).

**Command provenance**: Generated by the installed `speckit-plan` workflow on 2026-11-12. Constitution, Specify, and Clarify artifacts were not recreated; `spec.md` and `checklists/requirements.md` are preserved unchanged. **Corrective update 2026-11-12**: applied through the registered `speckit.plan` command path; see [reports/2026-11-12-plan-correction-receipt.md](./reports/2026-11-12-plan-correction-receipt.md).

## Summary

Deliver the complete journey **Import → Analyze → Detect Fields → Review → Fill → Save → Export** for scanned, non-fillable German PDF forms, using one Flutter/Dart codebase for Android and Web.

The architecture is a ports-and-adapters monorepo:

- **Platform-independent Dart** owns the document model, geometry, field recognition, form state, undo/redo, template logic, save/recovery coordination, export layout, and all user-facing German strings.
- **Android production adapters** (Kotlin, minimal and justified) own the Storage Access Framework import stream, PDF preflight, Android Keystore-backed encryption, on-device ML Kit OCR, PDFBox-Android flattening export, and system save/print/share. PDF rendering uses the native PDFium build through `pdfrx`.
- **Web development adapters** are deterministic and labeled `SIMULATED` for every capability (import source, page rasterization, secure storage, OCR, export, delivery). The browser rasterizer uses the real PDFium engine so geometry and visual findings transfer, but its results are still `SIMULATED` and never Android acceptance evidence.

The immutable imported PDF is copied once into app-private encrypted storage and becomes the rendering and export source of truth. User values are overlays in a versioned, UI-independent model and are flattened onto the original pages at export; original page content is never re-rendered or reconstructed.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13 / Flutter 3.47 (single codebase for Android and Web); Kotlin 2.x only for Android platform integration; Gradle Kotlin DSL.

**Primary Dependencies**:
- Flutter/Dart: `flutter_riverpod` (MIT) for injectable state and ports, `go_router` (BSD-3) for web-addressable navigation, `pdfrx` 2.12.0 (MIT, PDFium BSD-3) for page rendering on both platforms, `image` (MIT) for page-raster analysis, `pdf` ^3.11 (Apache-2.0) only for the `SIMULATED` web export artifact, `printing` (Apache-2.0) for Android print preview, `share_plus` (BSD-3) for the Android share sheet, `flutter_localizations` + gen-l10n (BSD-3) with German as the only release locale.
- Android native: `com.tom-roush:pdfbox-android:2.0.27.0` (Apache-2.0) for preflight, text/font metrics, and flattening export; bundled ML Kit Text Recognition v2 Latin (`google_mlkit_text_recognition` 1.0.2 wrapper, MIT; bundled Google model, proprietary but free, fully on-device, no telemetry) for OCR; Android Keystore AES-256-GCM for key wrapping; SAF `ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT` and `ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT`; `PrintManager`; `FileProvider`.
- Bundled font: Noto Sans Regular/Bold (SIL OFL 1.1) with precomputed glyph-advance metrics JSON, so text measurement is identical in Dart and PDFBox.
- No analytics, crash reporting, ads, cloud OCR, remote config, or network SDK of any kind. Full dependency rationale and rejected alternatives: [research.md](./research.md).

**Storage**: App-private internal storage (`filesDir`), no database. Immutable encrypted objects with an append-only revision model:
- `docs/<documentId>/meta.fx1`, `head.fx1`, `rev/<revisionId>.fx1`, `src/<sourceId>.fxc` (encrypted original PDF), `sig/<assetId>.fxs` (encrypted signature PNG).
- `templates/<templateId>/…` with immutable `ver/<versionId>.fx1` versions.
- AES-256-GCM, 1 MiB chunk framing, per-object 256-bit data key generated by `SecureRandom` and wrapped by a non-exportable Android Keystore master key; AAD binds file ID, chunk index, chunk count, and plaintext length.
- Atomic commit: temp file → fsync → read-back decrypt + SHA-256 verify → rename → atomically replace `head.fx1` → read-back verify. A save is reported successful only after the new head is readable. Stale `tmp/` is swept on startup.
- `android:allowBackup="false"`, `dataExtractionRules` excluding all app data, and release manifest without `INTERNET`.

**Testing**:
- `dart test` / `flutter test` for shared packages: model round-trips, geometry at zoom levels 0.5×–8×, date/number validation, undo/redo, autosave debounce and lifecycle, template independence, export layout and clip detection.
- `flutter test --platform chrome` + `integration_test` on Chrome with Chromium driver for the real editor journey on deterministic fixtures.
- Android `integration_test` on an exclusively allocated Orca emulator, plus Kotlin instrumentation tests for SAF import, Keystore loss, ML Kit offline OCR, PDFBox export, interrupted writes, and storage exhaustion.
- Independent artifact verification with at least two unrelated engines outside the app: Poppler (`pdftoppm`) and MuPDF (`mutool draw`), plus `qpdf --check`; the in-app PDFium preview provides a third view. Rendered-page pixel comparison against expected overlays; text-extraction checks for German characters.
- Accessibility: Flutter semantics tests, 200% text-scale tests, contrast checks, TalkBack walkthrough on emulator.
- Evidence is always reported as `SIMULATED`, `EMULATOR`, or `DEVICE` per constitution Principle VIII.

**Target Platform**: Android 8.0+ (`minSdk 26`, `compileSdk`/`targetSdk` 36) for production; Chrome 120+ on desktop for the development/validation surface. iOS is out of scope.

**Project Type**: Mobile app with a shared Web development surface — Flutter monorepo (`apps/` + `packages/` + `tools/`).

**Performance Goals**:
- Field detection: ≤ 3 s median per typical A4 page on the named representative device **Samsung Galaxy A54 5G (Exynos 1380, 6 GB RAM, Android 14, One UI 6.1)**, 200 DPI analysis raster, release build, measured by the in-app benchmark harness and reported with corpus/build/device metadata (SC-004).
- First page visible after document open: ≤ 700 ms on the same device; page-turn render ≤ 400 ms at fit-width zoom; overlay drag/resize at 60 fps (16.7 ms frame budget).
- Autosave commit (typical ≤ 2 MB revision): ≤ 300 ms; status reflects "saved" only after read-back verification.
- Two-page export including verification: ≤ 5 s on the same device.
- Peak memory ≤ 300 MB for a five-page A4 document at 200 DPI analysis and fit-width rendering; hard import cap 80 MiB per PDF (source bytes + PDFium document + one render/analysis bitmap fit the budget).
- The emulator profile **Pixel 7, API 35, x86_64, 4 GB RAM** is used for routine automated runs; emulator timings are not used for the performance claim.

**Constraints**:
- Fully offline core journey; release APK must not request `INTERNET` (debug-only manifest overlay may add it for hot reload). Web development assets (`pdfium.wasm`, CanvasKit, fonts) are served locally; no CDN at runtime.
- No plaintext document bytes in logs, caches, thumbnails, temp files, or backups. Decrypted page bytes exist only in bounded process memory for rendering/OCR/export; best-effort zeroization on release. Export preview files live only in app-private cache for the duration of the preview and are swept on startup/session end.
- Source PDF is immutable and never re-rendered; geometry in PDF points in source-page display space; no device-pixel arithmetic in the model.
- All release UI strings German; simulated results labeled `SIMULATED` in UI, logs, and reports; production adapter registry refuses to resolve a simulated adapter.
- Release APK budget ≤ 120 MB (bundled ML Kit model, PDFium, PDFBox, Noto Sans); measured on the release build and reported with the device evidence.
- No template is created implicitly; no stored user data is deleted to reclaim space.
- Paid hosted CI is not required; all mandatory checks must run on the local/self-hosted toolchain.

**Scale/Scope**: Single user per device; at least 50 stored documents/templates listed without search (FR-100); typical 1–10 pages and 20–150 fields per form, supported up to 100 pages and 500 fields per document; at least 20 rights-cleared real German authority forms plus synthetic CI fixtures in corpus `corpus-1.0.0`; German authority-form layouts only.

| **III. Android Is the Authoritative Platform** | PASS | Capability matrix assigns import, permissions, OCR, secure storage, lifecycle, and final PDF handling to real Android adapters. Physical-device acceptance remains a separate, explicitly recorded evidence class. |
| **IV. Automatic Field Recognition** | PASS | Hybrid geometry-first detection in pure Dart using ruling lines, boxes, whitespace, table cells, alignment, and label anchoring; OCR is auxiliary. | **V. Document Integrity and Reliable Export** | PASS | Encrypted immutable source copy; UI-independent versioned model; geometry in source-page points; values as overlays; export appends overlay content to imported pages and never re-renders them; artifact-level verification in two independent readers; clipping/misplacement/checkbox/signature defects block acceptance; templates stored separately and value-free. |
| **VI. Privacy, Security, and Offline Operation** | PASS | On-device bundled OCR; no network permission in release; no telemetry; Keystore-bound non-exportable key material and AES-GCM at rest; plaintext lifetime/location/cleanup defined; fixtures synthetic or rights-cleared; deletion and key-loss behavior specified in German. |
| **VII. Data Safety and User Control** | PASS | Template creation only via explicit action; derived documents pin template version IDs; no silent deletion; atomic saves with read-back; explicit German storage-full, key-unavailability, and deletion messaging; unsaved state surfaced as at risk. |
| **VIII. Testability and Evidence** | PASS | Unit/widget/browser/instrumentation/e2e layers; separate evidence classes; named device and emulator with build mode and corpus metadata; artifact verification; failure-case tests for key loss, storage exhaustion, interrupted writes, corrupt/encrypted input, failed recognition, rejected export; accessibility tested; German string completeness checked. |
| **IX. Official Spec Kit Development** | PASS | This plan is produced by the installed `speckit-plan` workflow with provenance recorded; existing spec, clarifications, and checklist are preserved. No manual recreation of earlier stages. No git branch/commit/publication is performed, per owner instruction. |
| **X. Autonomous Multi-Agent Governance** | PASS | Plan defines isolated worktree execution, candidate-revision-pinned independent review, author/reviewer separation, integration verification, and escalation for unattainable gates. This agent does not self-approve implementation. |
| **Architecture and Platform Constraints** | PASS | Single framework, shared core, explicit ports for import/OCR/storage/rendering/export, versioned model, encrypted app-private storage separated by kind, rights-cleared corpus, justified dependencies, scope discipline. |

Task generation, analysis, implementation, review, integration, and convergence remain future gates. |

**Structure Decision**: Flutter monorepo with one application and nine shared Dart packages. Shared packages contain no `dart:io` and no platform plugin imports, so the same sources compile for Android and Web. Android capability code lives in the app's Kotlin integration layer (not a parallel app) behind the single `FeldexaPlugin` facade. Web substitutes deterministic adapters in `feldexa_adapters_simulated`; the app bootstrap selects exactly one registry, and release builds fail fast if a simulated capability descriptor is present.

Package boundaries exist to keep core logic platform-free and independently testable (no package is introduced for a future feature): `feldexa_core` and `feldexa_export` have no Flutter dependency; `feldexa_ports` contains interfaces only; `feldexa_application` orchestrates use cases; `feldexa_ui` owns widgets/semantics; the two adapter packages are the only platform bindings; `feldexa_testkit` is test-only and never imported by production code.

## Architecture Decisions (summary; full rationale in research.md)

1. **Immutable encrypted source, overlay-only export.** The original PDF is copied once into encrypted app storage and never rewritten. Export imports those pages byte-for-byte into a new PDF and appends overlay content streams (text, checkbox vectors, signature image), then verifies and flattens.
2. **PDFBox-Android is the authoritative PDF engine.** PDFium (via `pdfrx`) is render-only; PDFBox supplies preflight, encryption detection, font metrics, overlay writing, and artifact verification. Independent artifact checks use Poppler and MuPDF outside the app, plus the in-app PDFium preview.
3. **Keystore-held wrapping key, chunked AES-GCM.** Data keys are generated with `SecureRandom` and wrapped by a non-exportable Keystore AES key; files are chunk-authenticated so multi-megabyte PDFs stream without whole-file plaintext and truncated/tampered chunks fail deterministically.
4. **Geometry in source-page points.** Every field rectangle is stored in points relative to the page's display box (CropBox after `/Rotate`), never in device pixels or normalized fractions. One shared mapper converts to view and PDF user space.
5. **Geometry-first recognition, OCR-assisted.** Pure-Dart analysis of ruling lines, boxes, table grids, whitespace, alignment, and label proximity generates candidates; OCR blocks supply label identity and numeric/date hints. No classifier training, no network, fully deterministic.
6. **One text layout engine.** Bundled Noto Sans plus a generated glyph-advance table means Dart layout and PDFBox drawing use identical metrics; overflow blocks export instead of silently shrinking or clipping text.
7. **Revisioned file store, no database.** Per-document encrypted metadata + immutable revision files + atomic head pointer; simpler failure semantics than a database for this scope and naturally separates documents, templates, and signature assets.
8. **Explicit capability registry.** `feldexa_ports` defines every platform capability; Android and Web registries are selected at compile time via conditional imports. A production-build assertion rejects simulated adapters.
9. **SIMULATED labeling is structural.** Simulated adapters return `CapabilityEvidence.simulated`, which the UI banner, structured logs, test reports, and evaluation output consume. There is no unlabeled path.
10. **Failure injection is a first-class port.** Clock, filesystem-quota, keystore availability, and write-interruption faults are injectable, so recovery, atomicity, and destructive-cleanup guarantees are tested rather than asserted.

## Risks and Mitigations

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bundled ML Kit model fails to load offline or adds unexpected network behavior | Core privacy/offline guarantee breaks | Verify bundled dependency variant; instrumented test with network disabled asserts OCR success and zero sockets; remove INTERNET from release manifest; dependency review gate |
| Detection quality below 90% on real forms | Product promise unmet | Geometry-first cues independent of OCR; frozen corpus measured early (Phase C dry run); correction workflow is the fallback; tuning driven only by measured failures |
| 3 s A4 budget missed with ML Kit + raster analysis | Performance target unmet | 200 DPI analysis raster (not 300), downscaled binarization, line detection on integral images, OCR only on page once, isolate-based pipeline, per-stage timing harness on Galaxy A54 |
| PDFBox overlay rendering differs from UI layout | Clipped/misplaced values | Shared font metrics table; contract test comparing Dart widths against PDFBox `getStringWidth`; artifact verification with pixel comparison and 1 mm tolerance |
| Multi-megabyte encryption cost blocks UI | Perceived slowness, autosave jank | Chunked AES-GCM in native worker; autosave serialized off the UI isolate; debounce 2 s; measured commit budget 300 ms |
| Key loss / backup expectations | Unrecoverable user work, trust loss | Pre-emptive German disclosure, specific key-loss error, per-document isolation, failure-injection tests |
| Kotlin surface grows into a parallel app | Constitution violation | Single `FeldexaPlugin` facade; services limited to platform capabilities; no UI in Kotlin; review checklist enforces the boundary |
| Web adapter leaks into production | Simulated data presented as real | Compile-time conditional registry; release assertion; no simulated package import in Android registry; build test inspects the resolution graph |
| Mixed page sizes/rotations misplace fields | Export defects | Per-page display box and rotation normalization; geometry property tests across rotations 0/90/180/270, CropBox offsets, mixed sizes |
| Plaintext export previews persist | Privacy violation | Cache-only preview with session-scoped lifetime, startup sweep, `allowBackup=false`, no thumbnails/logging of content |

## Evidence Plan

| Evidence class | Environment | What it can prove | What it can never prove |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SIMULATED` | Chrome + deterministic fixtures and simulated adapters | Editor interaction, overlay geometry, zoom/page navigation, responsive layout, filling, accessibility semantics, state logic | Any Android runtime behavior, real OCR quality, real storage/encryption, real export artifact validity |
| `EMULATOR` | Orca-allocated Pixel 7 API 35 (exclusive session) | Android integration behavior: SAF import, Keystore crypto, ML Kit offline OCR, PDFBox export, lifecycle, storage faults, system save/share/print flows | Physical-device performance claims, hardware-backed key strength on specific silicon, real-device acceptance |
| `DEVICE` | Samsung Galaxy A54 5G (Exynos 1380, 6 GB, Android 14) or owner-approved equivalent | 3 s A4 timing claim, real touch journey, device acceptance, offline/airplane-mode journey | Nothing beyond the tested device/build/corpus; results are cited with those conditions |

**Definition-of-Done alignment**: the milestone is not complete until the full journey works on the authoritative Android runtime, German UI/error/recovery paths are present, offline operation is demonstrated, export is artifact-verified, privacy/data-safety failure cases are tested, evidence is separated, and the integrated revision has passed independent review.

## Complexity Tracking

| Complexity | Why Needed | Simpler Alternative Rejected Because |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Minimal Kotlin integration layer (~8 services behind one channel) | Import streaming without plaintext cache, non-exportable Keystore keys, bundled ML Kit OCR, PDFBox flattening, and Android system delivery flows cannot be implemented in pure Dart | Pure-Dart `file_picker`+`cryptography` copies plaintext into caches and keeps exportable key material; a PDFium-only Dart path cannot write overlays; a parallel native UI is forbidden by Principle II |
| Custom chunked AES-GCM container (`FXC1`) | Multi-MB PDFs must be authenticated, streamed, atomically committed, and tamper-detected without whole-file plaintext | SQLCipher only encrypts a database and would force large blobs into one; Jetpack `EncryptedFile`/`EncryptedSharedPreferences` are deprecated/limited and give weaker failure semantics; whole-file AES-GCM doubles memory and loses partial-write detection |
| Dual adapter registries with a simulated implementation of every platform port | Constitution mandates Web-first development with deterministic substitutes and forbids production resolution of simulated adapters | A single registry with runtime platform checks risks shipping simulated code paths and cannot compile the Web build without Android plugins |
| PDFium **and** PDFBox as two PDF engines | PDFium is a superior renderer but cannot author; PDFBox can preflight, measure, write, and flatten but is not the UI renderer | A single engine would either lose export capability or degrade rendering and Web parity; using two also yields independent artifact verification |
| Bundled font metrics table generated from the TTF | Clipping warnings must match the export renderer exactly on both platforms | Runtime platform font measurement differs between Android, Web, and PDFBox; auto-shrinking text is prohibited by the spec |
